title: Hegseth Announces 20% Cut to Generals and Admirals, New Robotics Command
summary:
U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Wednesday that the military will cut 20% of its generals and admirals. He made the announcement in what he called his "state of the force" address at Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia. He spoke to junior officers and enlisted leaders.

Last spring, Hegseth ordered a 10% reduction in roughly 800 flag and general officer positions. He has now directed all of the military services to double that cut, for a total of 20%, to be finished by Jan. 1, 2027. "I call it accountability and long overdue," he said.

Hegseth also announced a new four-star command to oversee autonomous and robotic capabilities, which he called "the fastest peacetime shift in modern military history." He named an effort to study the future of warfare, led by Elon Musk, former House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Palmer Luckey, co-founder of Anduril Industries. Hegseth said the work "will be focused on discovering, developing and fielding the weapons and systems that our children and our grandchildren will need in their lifetimes." Musk's companies compete for government contracts, and last year President Donald Trump put him in charge of a federal cost-cutting effort. Democrats have said they would like to question Musk about what they see as the failures of that effort.

The Pentagon chief also led with changes aimed at what he calls "woke" culture, including a rollback of diversity programs and a review of ground combat units with female troops.

The speech came seven months into a war with Iran. The U.S. and Iran are in a stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital energy shipping route. Hegseth repeated claims that the U.S. military has destroyed Iran's navy, air force and defence systems, while Iran has continued to launch drone and missile attacks intermittently.

Members of Congress had mixed reactions to the cuts. Some called them a "purge" of the military's top ranks that will take years to rebuild. Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly, a former navy combat pilot who has been critical of Hegseth, said, "He's purging a generation of great leaders of the military, and it's going to take a generation to recover from it." Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said he wanted to understand Hegseth's reasoning. "If it's simply a matter of eliminating a very heavy top, there may be some validity to it, but I want to see it first," Rounds said.
why_it_matters: The story shows how large changes to the military's leadership and technology can draw different reactions from officials and lawmakers. It also shows why people ask for the reasoning behind major decisions during a time of war.

questions.question: What did Hegseth direct the military services to do with last spring's reduction?
options: Cancel it before the deadline
Double it, for a total of 20%
Cut it in half to 5%
Keep it at 10% for another year
questions.correct_answer: Double it, for a total of 20%

questions.question: What did the article say the new four-star command will oversee?
options: The review of ground combat units
The training of junior officers
The supply of weapons to allies
The rollout of autonomous and robotic capabilities
questions.correct_answer: The rollout of autonomous and robotic capabilities

questions.question: Who will lead the effort to study the future of warfare?
options: Mark Kelly, Mike Rounds and Pete Hegseth
Elon Musk, Newt Gingrich and Palmer Luckey
Newt Gingrich, Mike Rounds and Palmer Luckey
Donald Trump, Elon Musk and Mark Kelly
questions.correct_answer: Elon Musk, Newt Gingrich and Palmer Luckey

A stalemate
A trade deal
A shipping holiday

options: As purging a generation of great leaders
